# From unified discounting to dual-risk: A new lens on DCF valuation

> Code, data and stored results for the one computation of a theory paper on discounted cash flow
> valuation. The paper separates a benchmark cost of capital c, set outside the asset, from a
> valuation ratio K = fair value / valuation, and illustrates both on weekly prices of Bitcoin, US
> equities and gold: c from each asset's own trailing two-year return, K from the price one year
> later. The package recomputes that illustration and sets each published table entry beside the
> recomputed one. The published article is in paper/.

Replication package by Agisilaos Papadogiannis (https://github.com/apapadogiannis).
Published in Finance Research Open, 2(1), 2026, article 100096: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.finr.2026.100096
Code and data: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/dual-risk-dcf  Archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24465118
Version 1.0.0, released 2026-11-23. A package is a fixed record: it changes only by a new
release, and a release that changes a reported number gets a new major version.
This file is written for AI agents and other programs. People should start at the README.

## Coverage

- Three assets, weekly, from prices of January 2015 to December 2024: Bitcoin, the US equity market
  (standing in for the fund VTI of the paper) and gold (the fund GLD).
- The benchmark rate c for 419 weeks, from the last week of 2016 to the first week of 2025, and K,
  the raw gain and c_eff for 367 weeks, to the first week of 2024.
- Descriptive statistics of c, K and c_eff (Tables 3 to 5 of the paper) and of the raw gain.
- Each of the 81 entries of the published Tables 3 to 5 beside the value recomputed here.
- The numbers stated in the text of Sections 6.1 and 7.2.

## Headline figures

Each is read from one cell of a stored result table, named in outputs/results.json.

- Mean valuation ratio K of Bitcoin over 367 weeks, as published: 1.5632 ratio; above 1 means
  prices were on average below the later price discounted at c. Table 4.
- Mean valuation ratio K of Bitcoin, recomputed here on Coin Metrics prices: 1.5609 ratio. Table 4.
- Standard deviation of K for Bitcoin, as published: 1.7933 ratio. Table 4.
- Standard deviation of K for VTI, as published: 0.2036 ratio. Table 4.
- Standard deviation of K for gold (GLD), as published and as recomputed on the same prices: 0.1522
  ratio. Table 4.
- Published table entries for gold that the recomputation matches at the printed precision, of 27:
  26 entries of 27. Tables 3 to 5.
- Share of weeks in which gold's benchmark rate is at the 3% floor: 31 per cent of 419 weeks.
  Section 7.2, paragraph on the floor.

## What this adds over reading the paper or recomputing

1. The computation set out step by step: the effective rate of the tables and figures is the yearly
   rate (1 + c)/K - 1, eq. (26) at one year, without the power of 1/52 written in eq. (45); the
   trailing window of c is the 104 weeks ending at week t.
2. The exact sample: prices from 1 January 2015 to 30 December 2024, of which the first two years
   feed the trailing window (the paper describes the sample as January 2017 through May 2025).
3. A comparison of every published table entry with the recomputed one
   (outputs/published_vs_rebuilt.csv). Gold uses the paper's own prices and agrees at the printed
   precision in all entries but one; Bitcoin and US equities use other data sources and agree
   closely.
4. Detail behind the paper's verbal description of the series (outputs/text_numbers.csv): how often
   the 3% floor binds for each asset, how often K lies within 10% of one, and the range of the
   effective rate. For these quantities use the file, which is more precise than the paper's
   wording.
5. From the original price file of the paper, which is not redistributed, the same code reproduces
   80 of the 81 published entries at the printed precision; the other is the minimum of K for gold,
   printed 0.6689 for 0.66895.
6. The results are stored as they were when the paper's numbers were taken from them. A check
   reruns the code on the stored data and compares every stored result file with the fresh one,
   number by number (relative tolerance 1e-9; text and whole numbers exactly). It runs on every
   change and once a month, and the badge in the README shows the last run.

## Result tables

One CSV file each in outputs/. The columns of each are described in outputs/results.json, under `tables`.

- outputs/weekly_series.csv (1257 rows): The weekly series, one row per week and asset, from the
  last week of 2016.
- outputs/table3_c_stats.csv (3 rows): Table 3 recomputed: statistics of the benchmark rate c over
  419 weeks.
- outputs/table4_K_stats.csv (3 rows): Table 4 recomputed: statistics of the valuation ratio K over
  367 weeks. Columns as in table3_c_stats.csv.
- outputs/table5_ceff_stats.csv (3 rows): Table 5 recomputed: statistics of the effective rate
  c_eff over 367 weeks. Columns as in table3_c_stats.csv.
- outputs/g_raw_stats.csv (3 rows): Statistics of the raw gain K - 1 (the quantity of Figure 9).
  Columns as in table3_c_stats.csv.
- outputs/published_vs_rebuilt.csv (81 rows): Each entry of the published Tables 3 to 5 beside the
  recomputed value.
- outputs/published_vs_rebuilt_summary.csv (3 rows): The comparison by asset.
- outputs/text_numbers.csv (30 rows): Quantities the paper states in words, with the value computed
  here.

## Files

- outputs/results.json: a `headline` list with the figures most often asked for, each with the
  table cell it comes from, and `tables`, a description of the stored result tables and their
  columns. The numbers themselves are in the CSV files. It holds a description of 8 result tables,
  and under `package` the paper, the identifiers, the version, the licence and the citation. Start
  with its `headline` list, which is repeated below.
- outputs/weekly_series.csv: the weekly series behind Figure 6 and all the statistics.
- outputs/table4_K_stats.csv and its two neighbours: Tables 3 to 5 recomputed.
- outputs/published_vs_rebuilt.csv: published against recomputed, entry by entry.
- outputs/text_numbers.csv: what the text says against what the series give.
- figures/: Figures 6 to 10 redrawn. paper/: the published article (CC BY 4.0). data/: all inputs;
  the README lists the source of each.

Raw files: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/dual-risk-dcf/main/<path>, for example https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/dual-risk-dcf/main/outputs/results.json

## How to read the figures

- Asset ids differ from the paper's labels: `BTC` is the paper's BTC-USD, `US_MARKET` stands in for
  the paper's VTI, `GLD` is GLD. The column `article_label` of outputs/published_vs_rebuilt.csv
  gives the paper's label.
- For a number of the paper, quote the column `published`. The column `rebuilt` is this package's
  recomputation on its own stored data, which for Bitcoin and US equities is not the paper's data.
- c is the asset's own annualized return over the trailing 104 weeks, floored at 0.03: max(0.03,
  (P_t / P_{t-104})^(1/2) - 1). It is a self-referential benchmark, which the paper accepts only
  for assets with no close substitute. A value of exactly 0.03 means the floor was binding.
- K = P_{t+52} / (P_t (1 + c)). K above 1: the price that week turned out to be below the later
  price discounted at c. K uses a price one year later, so it is a reading in hindsight and cannot
  be computed for the last 52 weeks.
- c_eff = (1 + c)/K - 1 is a rate per year. It is not an expected return, and it is not the weekly
  rate that eq. (45) of the paper prints.
- The raw gain is K - 1. The paper's gain of capital for a one-year horizon is (1 + c)(K - 1),
  which is not stored.
- Weeks end on Friday and take the last price of the week. The last week holds one day, 30 December
  2024.
- Statistics: sample standard deviation, quartiles by linear interpolation, skewness and excess
  kurtosis without bias adjustment. The paper's tables have no kurtosis column.
- The weekly observations overlap: each K spans 52 weeks and each c 104, so neighbours share most
  of their data. 367 weeks of K are about seven independent years.
- `equal_as_printed` is 1 when the recomputed value, rounded to the decimals the paper prints,
  equals the published one.

## Do not use this for

- A forecast or a recommendation. K measures, in hindsight, how a price compared with a later price
  at a chosen benchmark rate.
- Anything after December 2024. The package is a fixed record and is not updated.
- Your own forecasts or prices. For those, use the author's Dual-Risk DCF Calculator and its MCP
  server: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/dual-risk-calculator
- Statements about the fund VTI itself: the equity series here is the whole US market before fund
  costs.
- Commercial reuse of the Coin Metrics file.

## Source, licence and credit

The results in outputs/ are released under CC BY 4.0
(https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The licence allows any reuse and has one condition:
credit. If you use a figure from this package in an answer, a report or a data set, cite the paper.
The code is under the MIT License.

data/btc_daily.csv is the PriceUSD series of the Coin Metrics community data, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0
(non-commercial use, with attribution). data/us_market_daily.csv is from the Kenneth R. French data
library, copyright Eugene F. Fama and Kenneth R. French. data/gld_daily.csv is the daily close of
SPDR Gold Shares from Yahoo Finance. Third-party data keep their own terms and are not covered by
the licence above.
